title: Oath and Veil
premise: In the city of Corvane, where magic was outlawed after the kingdom of Veilmark was erased from every map and memory, debt-bound temple scribe Marguerite Voss sells forbidden charms to survive. When a mute child arrives at her door speaking the dead language of Veilmark, Marguerite discovers she can understand it — proof that her own erased past is tied to the vanished country. Hunted by the Inquisitor who holds her debt and guided by a disgraced oath-keeper named Sera, Marguerite must find the Last Door before the child's borrowed time runs out. She ends her debt by sacrificing her recorded identity, walking through the Door as the country's final citizen, and choosing love for Sera over the restored life the Door offers her.
about_author: Astrid Oyelaran is a former archivist who writes fantasy about people trapped by paperwork, oaths, and other binding magic. She lives between two cities and claims neither, which she insists is research.

chapters.title: The Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. We meet her selling charms in Corvane's night market, counting coins against the temple debt that owns her name. A routine sale goes wrong when an Inquisitor's clerk nearly catches her. Emotional beat: weary defiance; she survives by being small and unmemorable.

chapters.title: A Child at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A boy of about eight appears at her door at dawn, barefoot, silent, drawing spirals in the dust. When he speaks, Marguerite understands him — a language no one should know. Emotional beat: uncanny recognition; something long-buried stirs in her.

chapters.title: Words Before Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The boy, Tam, names things in the old tongue and objects respond faintly — a candle bends toward his voice. Marguerite realizes the outlawed magic isn't gone, only sleeping in words. Emotional beat: terror and wonder braided together.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Summons
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The temple summons her: someone reported strange sounds at her lodging. Inquisitor Halev questions her with courteous menace, reminding her the debt ledger holds her true name. Emotional beat: claustrophobic fear; her smallness is failing her.

chapters.title: Sera of the Broken Oath
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. A disgraced oath-keeper who once guarded Veilmark's borders tracks the old language to Marguerite's door. She offers protection in exchange for help finding the Last Door. Emotional beat: wary mutual need; two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Remembers
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Reading her own debt contract closely, Marguerite finds her name written in the old script beneath the trade-tongue — she is from Veilmark, and doesn't remember it. Emotional beat: vertigo of self-loss; identity as something that can be confiscated.

chapters.title: The Erasure
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera explains how Veilmark was unmade: not conquered, but edited out — its name struck from records until reality complied. Those inside were scattered, their memories traded as payment. Emotional beat: grief for a home neither woman can picture.

chapters.title: Running on Borrowed Time
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Tam begins to fade at the edges — he is made of the country's last unspent memory, and it is running out. They must reach the Last Door within weeks or he dissolves. Emotional beat: maternal urgency hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Temple
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. To find the Door they need the original erasure decree. Marguerite uses her scribe access to steal into the restricted archive. Emotional beat: transgressive thrill; the obedient debtor finally breaking rules.

chapters.title: Halev's Bargain
chapters.summary: Halev's POV. The Inquisitor catches Marguerite in the archive but offers a deal: deliver the child, and her debt is cleared. He reveals the temple profits from erased memories — including hers. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite refuses, lying to Halev's face with the fluency of three years of small deceptions. She flees with the decree fragment and burns her bridge to the temple forever. Emotional beat: liberation through ruin.

chapters.title: Road Through Unmapped Country
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The trio travels toward the borderlands where Veilmark used to be, following Tam's instinct. Villages here have holes in their histories, wells with no names. Emotional beat: melancholy wonder; the shape of absence.

chapters.title: The Oath-Keeper's Confession
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera admits she held the border the night of the erasure — and obeyed the order to stand aside. Her broken oath is why she can see what others forgot. Emotional beat: shame offered like a wound; trust deepens.

chapters.title: Tam Speaks
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Tam finally speaks in the trade-tongue: he remembers being many people, all the erased citizens folded into one child. He calls Marguerite by a name she almost recognizes. Emotional beat: heartbreak; the cost of forgetting made flesh.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Ford
chapters.summary: Halev's POV. Temple hunters corner them at a river crossing. Sera holds the line with half-forgotten border-magic while Marguerite escapes with Tam. Emotional beat: sacrifice and fury; loyalty tested against survival.

chapters.title: The Price of the Crossing
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Sera survives but is captured. Marguerite must choose: rescue Sera or reach the Door before Tam fades past saving. Emotional beat: agonizing division; love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: What I Would Give
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite realizes the Door opens only for a citizen paying a price: a recorded identity surrendered whole. Her debt ledger, her name, her place in Corvane — everything. Emotional beat: quiet clarity; the choice was always going to be this.

chapters.title: Storming the Quiet House
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Imprisoned in the temple's Quiet House, Sera expects nothing — then Marguerite walks in wearing a scribe's stolen robes, coming for her first. Emotional beat: astonished tenderness; being chosen over the mission.

chapters.title: The Last Door
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At the borderland hollow, the Door stands as a seam of silence. Halev arrives for a final confrontation; Sera holds him off while Marguerite pays her identity into the threshold with Tam's hand in hers. Emotional beat: climax — courage as surrender.

chapters.title: Citizen of Nothing
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Inside the threshold, Marguerite faces what the Door offers: restoration of Veilmark with herself as its remembered founder — if she stays. She instead releases the stored memories outward, letting the world remember, and steps back out unnamed. Emotional beat: renunciation as triumph.

chapters.title: Names Returning
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Across Corvane, people wake remembering streets, songs, a country. Halev's authority crumbles as the erasure decree unravels. Sera finds Marguerite — nameless, free, smiling. Emotional beat: flood of restitution; joy after long grief.

chapters.title: Oath Renewed
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. With no debt, no record, and no country demanding anything, Marguerite chooses freely: she swears a new oath, not to temple or crown, but to Sera and to Tam, now a boy with a history again. Emotional beat: warm resolution; love chosen over duty, duty remade as love.
